items.caption: Variables are created automatically as soon as HeishaMon publishes the corresponding topics.
Deactivated datapoints are hidden - object ID and archive data remain. New topics are only created while activated. Reorder rows by drag & drop - variables and links follow the order.

items.name: MQTTTopic
items.caption: MQTT base topic
Must match the base topic configured in HeishaMon's own web interface exactly. If it does not match, no data is received - without any error message here.

Temperature sensors (e.g. DS18B20) connected to the HeishaMon's 1-Wire bus are detected automatically once a reading is received and appear here for naming and activation. Deactivated sensors are hidden - object ID and archive data remain.

items.name: OneWireList
items.caption: 1-Wire sensors

Creates a grouped category tree (Operation, Heating, DHW, ...) with links to all active datapoints in the target category selected below - useful for a tidy WebFront navigation instead of one long flat list of variables under the instance. Without a selected target category, nothing is created. Links of deactivated datapoints are removed automatically.

items.name: CreateLinks
items.caption: Create link structure

items.name: LinksLocation
items.caption: Target category (required for the link structure to be created)

elements.caption: External energy meter (optional, for measured COP / performance factor)

items.caption: If an external energy meter (e.g. Shelly 3EM) measures the heat pump supply line, select its variables here. The module then calculates the measured COP and the daily performance factor from the meter readings.

items.name: PowerVariable
items.caption: Energy meter: active power of the heat pump (W)

items.name: EnergyVariable
items.caption: Energy meter: energy counter of the heat pump (kWh)

items.name: COPMinPower
items.caption: Minimum power for COP calculation
Below this power, COP (measured) reports 0 instead of a misleading ratio - protects against standby noise (typically a few watts).

Automatically archives the monitoring datapoints (power, flow/return/outside temperature, COP, defrost, compressor starts/hours) so time-series tiles like the NRG-Stack heat pump monitor can show day/week/month/year charts. Each variable is only activated once - if you later disable logging for a variable in the archive handler, it stays disabled.

items.name: ArchiveMonitoring
items.caption: Archive monitoring datapoints automatically

elements.caption: 🆕 Extra commands (optional, requires large HeishaMon board / heat pump "Optional PCB" setting)

items.caption: These are write-only commands - the heat pump does not report their state back, so the displayed value only reflects the last command sent, not a confirmation.

items.name: EnableExtraCommands
items.caption: Show extra command variables
SmartGrid mode digitally replicates the heat pump's native SG ready function (normally switched via physical dry contacts at the outdoor unit).
Only takes effect if the heat pump's own service setting "Optional PCB" is set to Yes with the appropriate function selected - a different setting than the native "SG ready" service menu.
The two relays on the large HeishaMon board switch up to 230V/5A - typically used for an external thermostat contact, a pump, or similar low-power devices.

actions.caption: Update variable names
actions.confirm: Renames variables that still carry an old default name to the current translation. Custom names remain untouched.
